dex.text: A knock-kneed chick, grey with a pink flush, standing on one leg in water that is far too salty for anyone sensible. It has not decided yet whether it is a bird or a rumour.
dex.fact: Flamingo chicks are born grey or white. They turn pink over a couple of years from the pigments in the brine shrimp and algae they eat. The Akrotiri Salt Lake in Cyprus fills with greater flamingos each winter.

dex.text: Tall, pink and burning with it. It sweeps its bent beak through the shallows with the air of a duchess stirring soup, and where it walks the water seems to glow at the edges.
dex.fact: A flamingo feeds with its head upside down, using its bent bill like a sieve to filter shrimp and algae out of the water. Its colour comes from carotenoid pigments in that food, the same family of colours that turns a carrot orange.
